note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

precepts.why:
“Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree.” Their altars overthrown, their pillars broken, their groves burned, their graven images hewn down. “Ye shall not do so unto the Lord your God.”

Ahaz did the very thing the law forbade. He “sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.” He made his son to pass through the fire “according to the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel.”

The nations’ places of worship were to be utterly destroyed, not imitated. Ahaz walked in the way of the kings of Israel and imitated them.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

precepts.why:
The priests “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

The true altar was made after the pattern of heavenly things given through Moses. Ahaz went to Damascus to meet the king of Assyria, saw a heathen altar he admired, and sent Urijah the priest “the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.” He traded the pattern shown in the mount for the fashion of the nations.

Then he moved the brasen altar from before the Lord, made the new altar the place of all the offerings, and kept the brasen altar “for me to enquire by.” Moses was warned to make all things according to the pattern, and Ahaz did the opposite.

precepts.text: Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel come up to war against Judah, and Ahaz buys Assyria's help, which slays Rezin.
precepts.point: The hatred carried straight through the history. Elisha would not even look toward the king of Israel and dealt only with Jehoshaphat of Judah, and later Pekah of Israel conspired with Rezin of Syria against Judah, which began the exile of the north by the Assyrian kings.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.” The northern kingdom conspired with Syria against Judah, their own brethren.

Ahaz sent to the king of Assyria, “I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, which rise up against me.” He took the silver and gold of the house of the Lord and sent it as a present, and the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, took it, “and slew Rezin.”

That conspiracy of Israel with Syria against Judah is what began the exile of the north by the Assyrian kings.
